LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.4: Oral Expression

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oral Expression. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to keep a routine?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home
2. appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORAL EXPRESSION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oral Expression helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ORAL EXPRESSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home

What this means
In this part you learn to apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Oral Expression” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Oral Expression.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oral Expression is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Oral Expression” in your own words using one local example. (skill: apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Oral Expression. (skill: appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oral Expression to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Oral Expression from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oral Expression: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Oral Expression?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to keep a routine?
2. How do non- verbal cues support oral communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oral Expression means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home.
5. Be able to: appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
